title: One transformation accounts for the differences between porcupine-fish and sunfish

fields.label: Label
fields.value: One transformation accounts for the differences between porcupine-fish and sunfish

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Deforming the coordinate grid of Diodon (concentric circles and approximately hyperbolic curves) yields the outline of the sunfish Orthagoriscus, so that a single integral transformation accounts for all their apparently separate external differences while leaving the head region nearly unchanged.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. XVII: On the Theory of Transformations, or the Comparison of Related Forms

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: And as such it accounts, by one single integral transformation, for all the apparently separate and distinct external differences between the two fishes.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter XVII, “On the Theory of Transformations, or the Comparison of Related Forms”; topic “Transformations of fish outlines”. Scope: Diodon and Orthagoriscus (Mola), and by extension related fish genera

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch17-11: resolvable-now, resolvability 0.82

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The pair, transformation class and predicted unchanged region are specific. Open images and scans permit standard geometric model comparison capable of confirming a compact mapping or exposing separate residual changes.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Register homologous outlines and landmarks of Diodon and Mola, fit Thompson's single smooth transformation, and compare residuals and complexity with modular transformations while separately testing head invariance.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Homologous external landmarks are limited.

Pose and inflation state of pufferfish alter outlines.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The claim is about two named forms, both of which are extensively photographed and present in museum collections. A pre-specified simple map with held-out landmarks is a standard test and can fail. That makes the external-transformation claim resolvable with existing images, with the usual caution that outline agreement is weaker than agreement of internal landmarks.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Landmark outlines and homologous external points of Diodon and Mola, fit one low-parameter transformation of the sort Thompson drew, and score held-out points, including whether the head stays nearly unmoved. The claim is supported if that single map predicts the held-out anatomy; a need for separate local warps of body regions would refute the integral-transformation account.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
A sufficiently flexible warp can map any two outlines, so the test has to freeze a simple transformation and hold landmarks out.

Individual and preservational variation in these deep-bodied fishes adds scatter around one diagrammatic map.
